name: supermodel
why: A Sega Model 3 arcade emulator, reverse-engineered hardware brought back to life; strange and excellent, though the formula is only lightly maintained.

brief.what_it_is: Supermodel is an emulator for Sega's Model 3 arcade platform, the 3D arcade hardware of 1996 to 1999. It uses OpenGL and SDL2 and runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS. It supports network play over low-latency connections. The source is GPL-licensed. The README does not mention the ppcd executable that the formula lists, so I could not describe it from these pages.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the aim is 'to develop an emulator that is both accurate and playable.' It notes that no public documentation for the Model 3 exists, so what is known 'has been painstakingly reverse engineered from scratch.'
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the emulation internals beyond the reverse-engineering effort. It describes the original hardware as having an on-board scene graph and geometry processor that could transform, light, and rasterize tens of thousands of polygons per frame at 57.524 fps.

brief.install_notes: Windows: the preferred route is MSYS2 with GCC and Make, plus SDL2 and SDL2_net from pacman. Visual Studio 2026 is also supported. Run the Get_Libs.cmd files in the libraries directory first, then build in the GUI or use the Build.cmd file in the MSVC folder. Linux: install SDL2, SDL2_net, and libglu1-mesa-dev through the package manager, then run make. macOS: install Xcode Command Line Tools. Then download the SDL2 and SDL_net .dmg files from their GitHub release pages and install them into /Library/Frameworks before running make. Prebuilt automated builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux are on the GitHub releases page, so building from source is optional. Game ROMs are not mentioned in the README.
brief.standout: It is a preservation project built from reverse engineering alone, since Sega never published Model 3 documentation. The README highlights network play, which is unusual for an arcade emulator.
brief.status: Maintained, per the README. The copyright line reads 2003-2026, it points to automated GitHub builds for three platforms, and it mentions a Visual Studio 2026 build path. The README gives no last-commit or release date, so I could not confirm recent activity directly. The scout note calls it lightly maintained, which this README does not support.
brief.caveats: The README says the project lost its web hosting and its forum, so Discord is now the main place for questions. Installing the macOS dependencies means manual .dmg installs. macOS users may need to grant execution permission to downloaded binaries through Finder's right-click Open. The README does not mention which game ROMs are needed or how to obtain them.

entry.title: Supermodel
entry.tldr: An emulator for Sega's Model 3 arcade boards, rebuilt entirely from reverse engineering because Sega never published documentation for the hardware.
entry.deeper_look:
Supermodel emulates the Model 3, Sega's 3D arcade platform from 1996 to 1999. It uses OpenGL and SDL2 and runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS. The README says it lets you "relive state-of-the-art 3D arcade gaming as it existed from 1996 through 1999."

The interesting part is how it got built. No public documentation for the Model 3 exists, so, in the README's words, what is known "has been painstakingly reverse engineered from scratch." The original hardware had an on-board scene graph and geometry processor that could transform, light, and rasterize tens of thousands of polygons per frame at 57.524 fps. Reproducing that behaviour from the outside, with no spec to check against, is the project's whole story.

The stated aim is "to develop an emulator that is both accurate and playable." Those two goals pull against each other, and watching a project balance them is a good way into emulation, hardware preservation, and what it takes to learn a machine nobody documented. It also supports network play over low-latency connections, which is unusual for an arcade emulator.

The formula also installs a second executable, ppcd. The README does not mention it, so this entry does not describe it.
entry.install:
brew install supermodel
# The README does not say which game ROMs are needed or how to get them. You supply those yourself.
